title: Environmental prevention and pharmacological prophylaxis for invasive fungal disease in pediatric high-risk cancer patients: experience from a large European cancer center.
summary:
This retrospective, single-center trial includes patients at high risk for developing IFD who were treated at the Department of Pediatric Hematology and Oncology of the Medical Center of the University of Freiburg, between 01 January 2016 and 30 August 2020, and between 01 October 2024 and 30 September 2025. Patients treated between September 2020 and September 2024 will be intentionally excluded from the study period, as extensive construction work for a new pediatric hospital in close proximity to the previous medical center could have led to an artificial increase in fungal spore concentrations and, consequently, to a transiently elevated incidence of invasive fungal infections. At the end of September 2024 patients were relocated in the new children hospital. Patients will be therefore grouped in two cohorts for further analysis: 2016 – 2020 cohort and 2024 – 2025 cohort, respectively before and after relocation of the hospital.
Every year, approximately 80 children and adolescents are diagnosed with cancer or relapse of a previous malignancy and receive treatment at the Department of Pediatric Hematology and Oncology of the University Children's Hospital of Freiburg. Of these, around 10 children per year exhibit risk factors predisposing to IFD. In addition, the department operates an accredited HSCT program, performing approximately 30 allogeneic HSCT procedures per year. 
Based on these estimates, we anticipate enrolling up to 200 patients, who are at increased risk for IFD.
conditions: Patients matching the codes for acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL, C91.0), acute myeloid leukemia (AML, C92.0), immunodeficiency (D84.9), myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS, D46), severe aplastic anemia (SAA, D61.9), HSCT (Z94.84) and prophylactic antifungal use (Z29.9).

interventions.name:
Eligible patients from the Department of Pediatric Hematology and Oncology will be identified using the department’s ICD-10 diagnosis registry and the department’s ICD-10 based database of prescribed antifungal medications. 
Patients will be included upon available informed consent.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Presence of (≥ 1) high-risk criteria for IFD according to ECIL-8 recommendations (Groll, Pana et al. 2021):
	AML and relapsed / refractory AML
	high-risk ALL and relapsed / refractory ALL
	chronic granulomatous disease and other immunodeficiencies requiring HSCT 
	myelodysplastic syndrome requiring HSCT
	refractory cytopenia of childhood (RCC) requiring immunosuppressive therapy or HSCT
	SAA requiring immunosuppressive therapy or HSCT
	any other disease requiring an allogenic HSCT
	persistent severe neutropenia (absolute neutrophile count (ANC) < 500/µL for > 10 days)
•	HSCT performed and / or intensive chemotherapy started between 01 January 2016 and 30 August 2020, and between 01 October 2024 and 30 September 2025.
•	Informed consent to Hilda Biobank
Exclusion criteria:
•	Absence of high-risk criteria for IFD 
•	Patients not treated within the above-mentioned time period
•	Absence of informed consent to Hilda Biobank
